status.en: 123 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 19% more than the week before, most of them in Gaza, Jerusalem and Hebron.
status.nb: 123 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 19 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Gaza, Jerusalem og Hebron.

summary.en: In the past week 139 armed incidents were reported, 30% more than the previous week, mainly in Gaza, Jerusalem and Hebron, and 50 of them were covered by two or more outlets. Battle‑related deaths in 2024 total 21 440 according to UCDP. Reports describe ongoing killings in Gaza a year into the cease‑fire, severe hunger and malnutrition, and large protests in Europe and London demanding an end to the war. Israeli actions include a building destroyed in Gaza and a rise to 17 in the number of Palestinian terror operatives killed by the IDF in the past week.
summary.nb: I løpet av den siste uken ble 139 væpnede hendelser rapportert, 30 % mer enn uken før, hovedsakelig i Gaza, Jerusalem og Hebron, og 50 av dem ble dekket av to eller flere medier. Kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024 er 21 440 ifølge UCDP. Rapporter beskriver pågående drap i Gaza ett år inn i våpenhvilen, alvorlig sult og underernæring, samt store protester i Europa og London som krever en slutt på krigen. Israels handlinger inkluderer en bygning ødelagt i Gaza og en økning til 17 i antall palestinske terroroperatører drept av IDF i den siste uken.

background.title: Gaza war
background.extract: The Gaza war is an armed conflict in the Gaza Strip and Israel, fought as part of the unresolved Israeli–Palestinian and Gaza–Israel conflicts. The war began on 7 October 2023, when Palestinian militant group Hamas led an attack on Israel, in which 1,195 Israelis and foreign nationals were killed and 251 were taken hostage. Since the start of the Israeli offensive that followed, over 74,000 Palestinians in Gaza have been killed; several studies in The Lancet indicate this figure is likely a significant undercount. Many scholarly sources and international organizations—including UN bodies, NGOs, and the International Association of Genocide Scholars—have concluded that Israel's actions in Gaza constitute genocide under international law. Several countries have also stated that genocide is occurring and have supported legal proceedings before the International Court of Justice. Israel and its supporters, including the United States, deny that genocide has occurred.
